title: Personal Checking: Refund Amount for an Extended Overdraft Fee Charged in Error
content:
## Statement of the combination

For the extended overdraft fee most recently posted to a Personal Checking account, one ground of error on its own settles that the fee is a bank error; the grounds do not have to hold together.

Where the fee is a bank error and no refund has yet been booked against it, it is returned whole, at the precise amount shown on the fee entry, with bank error recorded as the reason; a partial return is never made. Where a refund entry already exists against the fee, nothing more is returned. Where no ground holds, this policy returns nothing; an appeal for goodwill is a matter for the Personal Checking courtesy refund gates.

As fee amounts are held in dollars and cents, the refund involves no rounding.

## Grid

| Some ground holds | Refund entry already booked | Refund here |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | entire fee |
| yes | yes | none |
| no | no | none |
| no | yes | none |

## Hypothetical example

An extended overdraft fee of 22.00 USD, never refunded, rests on an episode whose opening debit a transfer would have paid: 22.00 USD is refunded as a bank-error correction.
